failed_tests.classification: new test added by 5b944211; outside the known clock-ordering files, so treated as potentially caused by the change; intermittent (failed in the suite and in 2 of 3 reruns alone)
failed_tests.observed: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable (the claim returned no job)
failed_tests.behaviour_pinned: A job whose created_at and available_at both lie 40 seconds in the future (as after a backward wall-clock step) was never delayed and must still be claimable under the new due condition available_at<=created_at OR available_at<=clock_timestamp().
failed_tests.observed_mechanism: The test sets both columns with two separate clock_timestamp() calls in one UPDATE. A probe against the run's database (temporary table, same UPDATE shape, 500 statements per order) gave available_at later than created_at by a sub-millisecond amount in 56 of 500 and 47 of 500 statements, equal otherwise, whichever column is named first in SET. When available_at is later than created_at, neither branch of the due condition holds, so the claim returns nothing. This was observed for the test's setup only; the job defaults in migrations use now(), which is constant within a transaction. Not established that this is the cause of every observed failure.
